claim_boundary.reason: This guide documents provenance mechanics only. It is not source evidence, model validation, scientist review, or production authorization.

common_mistakes: Hashing a file after editing it to fill CSV values.
Using MD5, SHA-1, or a truncated digest instead of full SHA-256.
Using an absolute private laptop path instead of a stable relative raw_sources path.
Changing source files after checksums were recorded.
Using a source with unreviewed, blocked, or unknown license scope.

package_layout.purpose: Reviewed source-governance manifest keyed by source_id and SHA-256 digest.
Immutable source package or source export used to compute source_ref digests.
Filled evidence CSV whose source_ref values match partner_source_manifest.json.

standards_anchors.name: NIST FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard
standards_anchors.use: Treat SHA-256 as the stable source integrity reference for partner evidence packages.

standards_anchors.name: Python hashlib documentation
standards_anchors.use: Use hashlib.sha256 for deterministic local checksum reproduction.

standards_anchors.name: GNU coreutils sha256sum
standards_anchors.use: Use sha256sum where GNU coreutils are available.

supported_reference_formats.use: Use when the CSV source_ref points directly to a reviewed source package digest.
Use when partners also provide a stable relative raw_sources path for review navigation.

workflow_steps: Freeze each raw source export or package before filling evidence CSV rows.
Compute the SHA-256 digest from the frozen source file or source package.
Add one partner_source_manifest.json source entry with sha256, owner, license, reviewer, reviewed_at, and evidence_package_ref.
Use the same digest in each CSV source_ref that depends on that source.
Run source-manifest validation, then full evidence validation, before scientist or claim review.
